decisions.title: Specification editions and codec delegation
decisions.issue: The wire specifications define distinct data models while maintained Go codecs expose overlapping subsets and defaults.
interpretations: Wrap pinned codecs with explicit package policy.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained Go and dependency codecs are compared where wrapper policy deliberately differs.
decisions.selected_behavior: Delegate syntax and Go value mapping to the pinned maintained codecs while keeping limits, options, and error classification in this package.
decisions.rationale: Delegation preserves maintained format implementations without claiming one lossless cross-format model.
decisions.security_consequences: Package preflight and bounded wrapper policy remain authoritative at hostile input boundaries.
decisions.resource_consequences: Finite package limits constrain codec work and allocation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Codec upgrades require decision and differential review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Each format retains its own data model and codec-defined representation within documented package policy.
decisions.upstream_status: Source editions and maintained codec versions are pinned and monitored separately.
decisions.reconsider_when: Any source edition, codec version, or supported format changes.

decisions.title: Complete input units and destination mutation
decisions.issue: Format documents do not define one uniform Go decoder policy for empty input, concatenated units, invalid targets, or partial destination mutation.
interpretations: Require exactly one complete unit with explicit stream APIs.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained-peer destination mutation after errors has not been assessed as a portable contract.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require one complete non-empty unit except for TOML's valid empty document, and treat destinations as indeterminate after decode errors.
decisions.rationale: A single-value API must not silently become a stream API or promise rollback it cannot provide.
decisions.security_consequences: Trailing or concatenated attacker-controlled data cannot be ignored.
decisions.resource_consequences: Readers stop at a bounded detection byte beyond the configured limit.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers needing streams must select the explicit YAML multi-document option or a future streaming API.
decisions.wire_consequences: Successful decode consumes exactly the documented format unit.
decisions.upstream_status: No cross-format standard defines destination rollback semantics.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separately owned streaming or transactional decode API is introduced.

decisions.title: Input, structural, graph, and output limits
decisions.issue: The wire formats permit values larger or deeper than a general service can safely process and do not select package resource budgets.
interpretations: Leave limits to callers or codecs.
Enforce finite format-aware input, structure, graph, and output limits.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained codec defaults vary and are not treated as a portable shared limit contract.
decisions.selected_behavior: Use finite defaults, validate negative limits, preflight format structure, and complete output within quota before writing.
decisions.rationale: Bounded work and all-or-error output are required at an untrusted serialization boundary.
decisions.security_consequences: Forged lengths, deep graphs, and oversized output are rejected before disproportionate work or partial emission.
decisions.resource_consequences: The default input and output budget is 1 MiB with explicit format-aware structural limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers may select stricter or documented larger limits without changing format semantics.
decisions.wire_consequences: Limit failures emit no partial encoded document.
public_apis: All bounded decode and encode APIs
decisions.upstream_status: Resource budgets remain package policy rather than CBOR or cross-format requirements.
decisions.reconsider_when: Measured service constraints justify a compatibility-reviewed default change.

decisions.title: Conservative format detection
decisions.issue: No supported format specification or HTTP semantics rule reliably discriminates all supported payload formats from bytes alone.
interpretations: Guess from names or media types.
Recognize only unambiguous leading JSON and XML shapes.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained-peer automatic detection has not been assessed because explicit format selection is the normal API.
decisions.selected_behavior: Detect only leading JSON objects or arrays and leading XML markup after whitespace, reporting every other payload as unsupported.
decisions.rationale: Scalar JSON, YAML, TOML, and binary formats overlap and cannot be guessed reliably.
decisions.security_consequences: The package does not execute multiple parsers speculatively on attacker-controlled input.
decisions.resource_consequences: Detection performs bounded leading-byte inspection only.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers must explicitly select every format outside the narrow JSON and XML shapes.
decisions.wire_consequences: SOAP is reported as XML and unknown or empty input remains unsupported.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9110 defines media types but no content-sniffing algorithm for these formats.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separate evidence-backed media-type boundary is introduced.

decisions.title: JSON names, numbers, Unicode, and normalization
decisions.issue: RFC 8259 recommends unique names, permits number-range variation, and requires UTF-8 on open ecosystems while Go accepts duplicate names and invalid UTF-8.
interpretations: Preserve first or last duplicate values.
Expose compatibility defaults with explicit strictness.
decisions.peer_behavior: Go encoding/json replaces invalid UTF-8 and uses last-value duplicate handling, which deliberately differs from strict package options.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require valid UTF-8, preserve Go numeric conversion, retain last-value duplicate compatibility by default, and provide recursive duplicate rejection explicitly.
decisions.rationale: The default preserves established Go compatibility while exposing a bounded strict boundary for ambiguous objects.
decisions.security_consequences: Strict mode prevents duplicate-member smuggling and invalid UTF-8 parser differentials.
decisions.resource_consequences: Duplicate detection and normalization remain bounded by input limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Existing last-value behavior remains available while strict consumers can reject duplicates before destination mutation.
decisions.wire_consequences: Normalize preserves number lexemes, orders keys, compacts whitespace, and strips only an initial UTF-8 BOM.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 8259 errata are monitored; no stricter duplicate-name requirement is adopted.
decisions.reconsider_when: A compatibility-governed profile changes the duplicate-name default or JSON source authority.

decisions.title: XML strictness, namespaces, entities, and charsets
decisions.specification: XML 1.0 Fifth Edition and Namespaces in XML 1.0 Third Edition
decisions.section: XML sections 2 through 4 and Namespaces sections 2 through 6
decisions.issue: Go exposes recovery and charset hooks while XML and Namespaces define syntax and expanded names without selecting this package's safe profile.
interpretations: Use strict resolved names and explicit charset conversion.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained-peer recovery, DTD, and charset behavior has not been assessed as a package interoperability guarantee.
decisions.selected_behavior: Use strict parsing, one root, resolved namespace names, finite depth, no declared entity expansion, and an explicit bounded charset allowlist.
decisions.rationale: Resolved names and explicit decoding avoid prefix, entity, and charset ambiguity at service boundaries.
decisions.security_consequences: DTD entity expansion and unbounded recovery are not enabled by default.
decisions.resource_consequences: Token depth and input bytes are bounded before recursive work.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Non-strict recovery and custom charset readers remain explicit opt-ins.
decisions.wire_consequences: Output follows encoding/xml traversal and does not claim XML canonicalization or lexical prefix preservation.
decisions.upstream_status: The dated XML and Namespaces editions are pinned and monitored independently.
decisions.reconsider_when: The Go XML contract, required charset set, or supported XML edition changes.

decisions.title: SOAP versions, envelope profile, and faults
decisions.specification: SOAP 1.1 and SOAP 1.2 Part 1 Second Edition
decisions.section: SOAP 1.1 section 4 and SOAP 1.2 sections 2 through 5
decisions.issue: SOAP 1.1 and 1.2 define different envelope and fault structures while processing, headers, and HTTP policy extend beyond a transport-neutral codec.
interpretations: Coerce both versions into one loose XML shape.
Expose a strict envelope profile with raw escape hatches.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained SOAP-stack behavior has not been assessed; local fixtures cover the selected transport-neutral profile.
decisions.selected_behavior: Select the version by namespace, require the defined envelope structure, preserve raw sections, and expose version-specific typed faults without owning HTTP or WS-* policy.
decisions.rationale: A narrow envelope codec avoids silently implementing an incomplete SOAP processing model.
decisions.security_consequences: Unexpected envelope structure and malformed raw fragments fail before application decoding.
decisions.resource_consequences: Envelope parsing and raw section copies remain bounded by package limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: SOAP 1.1 and 1.2 faults retain their distinct public fields and namespace rules.
decisions.wire_consequences: Typed bodies require exactly one child and valid faults return both the envelope and FaultError.
decisions.upstream_status: The dated SOAP 1.1 and SOAP 1.2 publications are pinned and monitored together.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separately specified processing or transport profile is added.

decisions.title: YAML schema, aliases, merges, duplicates, and streams
decisions.issue: YAML graphs, recommended schemas, aliases, tags, merge behavior, and multi-document streams do not map uniformly to native Go values.
interpretations: Adopt pinned v4 defaults with explicit defensive options.
decisions.peer_behavior: go.yaml.in/yaml/v4 is the maintained codec; the wrapper repairs a known invalid block-scalar indentation output.
decisions.selected_behavior: Use v4 defaults, one document and unique keys by default, sorted maps, finite protections, and explicit options for streams, aliases, and merges.
decisions.rationale: The package preserves YAML's supported model without claiming a JSON-compatible subset or unbounded graph support.
decisions.security_consequences: Duplicate keys, hostile aliases, and excessive depth are rejected by default protections.
decisions.resource_consequences: Alias, depth, input, and output limits bound processing.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Tags, implicit types, non-string keys, aliases, and merges remain documented codec-governed behavior.
decisions.wire_consequences: Multiple documents require an explicit slice target and opt-in; emitted mapping keys are sorted.
decisions.upstream_status: The YAML edition and maintained codec tags are monitored separately.
decisions.reconsider_when: The YAML edition, default schema, or codec behavior changes.

decisions.title: TOML document model and conversion
decisions.issue: TOML defines one document and native value types but not Go target conversion, unknown-field policy, or source-format preservation.
interpretations: Preserve native types and expose strict target validation.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained BurntSushi/toml behavior is delegated but no separate peer differential is currently assessed.
decisions.selected_behavior: Parse one complete document, preserve native date, time, and numeric types, reject lossy target conversion, and make unknown-field rejection explicit.
decisions.rationale: Typed conversion must not silently lose TOML value identity or numeric range.
decisions.security_consequences: Conflicting keys and incompatible target assignments fail instead of being normalized silently.
decisions.resource_consequences: Input and encoded output remain bounded by package limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: The valid empty document remains accepted and strict unknown-field checking stays opt-in.
decisions.wire_consequences: Encoding sorts map keys but does not preserve comments or original formatting.
decisions.upstream_status: TOML 1.1.0 and upstream tags are pinned and monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: The TOML edition or maintained codec changes.

decisions.title: MessagePack maps, extensions, numeric fit, and structure
decisions.issue: MessagePack defines encoded values but not duplicate-key handling, Go numeric narrowing, application extension ownership, or resource limits.
interpretations: Validate duplicates, numeric fit, structure, and extensions explicitly.
decisions.peer_behavior: github.com/vmihailenco/msgpack/v5 accepts duplicate map keys that the wrapper rejects by default.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require one object, reject recursive duplicates by default, validate typed numeric fit and structural limits, and reject unknown extensions.
decisions.rationale: Ambiguous maps, forged lengths, and lossy conversion are unsafe defaults for untrusted data.
decisions.security_consequences: Duplicate keys, unknown extensions, and hostile lengths fail before ambiguous assignment or allocation.
decisions.resource_consequences: Finite nesting and collection limits preflight declared sizes.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Last-key-wins compatibility and alternate struct or numeric modes remain explicit options.
decisions.wire_consequences: Encoders sort supported map keys and preserve registered timestamp behavior.
decisions.upstream_status: The exact format commit and maintained peer tags are monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: Extension ownership or the maintained codec contract changes.

decisions.title: CBOR deterministic profiles and accepted data items
decisions.section: RFC 7049 section 3.9, RFC 8949 section 4.2, and CTAP 2.2 section 8
decisions.issue: RFC 7049, RFC 8949, and CTAP2 define different deterministic profiles while tags, indefinite lengths, and accepted data items remain independently configurable.
interpretations: Accept every valid item by default.
Expose exact profiles and independent decode policy.
decisions.peer_behavior: github.com/fxamacker/cbor/v2 accepts duplicate keys under its generic default while the wrapper rejects them.
decisions.selected_behavior: Name the three exact deterministic profiles, reject duplicate keys, keep tags and indefinite lengths opt-in, and retain finite limits.
decisions.rationale: Profile names must preserve their source semantics instead of collapsing incompatible canonicalization rules.
decisions.security_consequences: Duplicate-key ambiguity and unbounded structures are rejected independently of profile selection.
decisions.resource_consequences: Input, nesting, collection, and output limits remain finite.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Legacy Canonical remains the encode default while other profiles require explicit selection.
decisions.wire_consequences: Decode does not claim that incoming bytes already satisfy any deterministic encode profile.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC errata, CTAP publications, and the maintained codec remain separately monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: Profile naming, minimum versions, or accepted data-item policy changes.

decisions.title: BSON document identity, order, duplicates, and conversion
decisions.issue: BSON defines ordered typed documents but does not select duplicate-name handling, Go map determinism, or lossy target conversion policy.
interpretations: Require one document and explicit ordered or compatibility representations.
decisions.peer_behavior: The maintained MongoDB Go driver preserves duplicate elements in ordered documents while the wrapper rejects them by default.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require one complete top-level document, reject recursive duplicates by default, preserve official driver types, and expose lossy conversions only as options.
decisions.rationale: Document identity and order must remain explicit and ambiguous duplicate data must not silently collapse.
decisions.security_consequences: Declared length, terminator, trailing bytes, and duplicate names are validated before assignment.
decisions.resource_consequences: Input and output remain bounded and forged lengths are rejected before large allocation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Ordered D and raw forms remain stable while unordered M output is explicitly non-deterministic.
decisions.wire_consequences: ObjectID string conversion, truncating doubles, integer minimization, and JSON tags are opt-in.
decisions.upstream_status: The BSON 1.1 publication and maintained driver are monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: The BSON edition or official driver type model changes.

decisions.title: Deterministic output is not universal canonicalization
decisions.issue: Some formats define deterministic profiles while others permit many equivalent serializations, so stable bytes cannot be called universally canonical.
interpretations: Describe determinism per format and value shape.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained-peer byte agreement has not been assessed as a cross-format guarantee.
decisions.selected_behavior: Claim sorted or stable output only for documented value shapes and name canonicalization only where an exact source profile exists.
decisions.rationale: Signing and hashing consumers must not infer a standards-level canonical form from incidental stable bytes.
decisions.security_consequences: The documentation avoids unsafe cross-format signing assumptions.
decisions.resource_consequences: Deterministic modes remain subject to the same bounded output policy.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Codec upgrades and formatting options remain compatibility-relevant even when semantic values are unchanged.
decisions.wire_consequences: XML is not C14N, BSON maps are unordered, and CBOR names the selected deterministic profile exactly.
decisions.upstream_status: Only CBOR sources define the named deterministic profiles used by this package.
decisions.reconsider_when: A signing use case or codec upgrade proposes a stronger byte-level guarantee.

decisions.title: Error classification, causes, and disclosure
decisions.issue: Codec errors mix syntax, conversion, limits, targets, protocol faults, and raw diagnostics without a shared stable package taxonomy.
interpretations: Wrap bounded causes in a stable cross-format taxonomy.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained-peer diagnostic disclosure has not been assessed as a portable contract.
decisions.selected_behavior: Classify stable error kinds while preserving errors.Is and errors.As causes without echoing complete payloads.
decisions.rationale: Callers need actionable classification without coupling to dependency text or leaking attacker-controlled data.
decisions.security_consequences: Complete payloads and tested sensitive values are not included in errors.
decisions.resource_consequences: Error construction does not add unbounded copies of input data.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Stable sentinels and typed errors remain usable across dependency error-shape changes.
decisions.wire_consequences: Valid SOAP faults remain protocol outcomes rather than malformed input.
decisions.upstream_status: The Go 1.26.6 errors contract and release stream are pinned and monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: A dependency error shape or disclosure boundary changes.

decisions.title: Encode graph validation and dependency differentials
decisions.issue: Recursive Go values can cycle or exceed stack-safe depth while maintained codecs may accept behavior that conflicts with package guarantees.
interpretations: Preflight active recursion paths and retain classified differentials.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained codec differences for invalid JSON UTF-8, duplicate maps, and YAML emission are recorded as executable evidence.
decisions.selected_behavior: Reject cycles on the active path and traversal beyond 1000 levels while allowing reused acyclic references and retaining classified codec differentials.
decisions.rationale: Package safety guarantees must be established before recursive dependency work without rejecting valid shared acyclic values.
decisions.security_consequences: Cyclic or excessively deep values fail before stack exhaustion or unbounded recursive encoding.
decisions.resource_consequences: Graph traversal has an explicit finite depth and active-path ownership model.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Known dependency differences remain deliberate package policy rather than hidden patches.
decisions.wire_consequences: Only validated acyclic values reach the selected format encoder.
decisions.upstream_status: The Go language edition and maintained codec versions are pinned and monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: A codec upgrade or new recursive value model changes graph behavior.

decisions.title: Transport, schema, and application boundaries
decisions.issue: Wire formats are often coupled to HTTP, media types, schemas, signing, persistence, and application mapping that no single format specification owns uniformly.
interpretations: Grow one serialization framework owning surrounding policy.
Remain a narrow composable format boundary.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained-peer framework scope has not been assessed because the decision defines this package's ownership boundary.
decisions.selected_behavior: Own bounded byte and reader or writer format handling only, leaving transport, schema, signing, compression, persistence, and application policy to composed layers.
decisions.rationale: A narrow boundary keeps unrelated standards and application lifecycle policy out of a codec package.
decisions.security_consequences: Callers must validate media, schema, compression, signature, and trust policy at their owning boundaries.
decisions.resource_consequences: Only codec-owned input, output, and structure budgets are enforced here.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: New surrounding capabilities require separately specified additive APIs and decisions.
decisions.wire_consequences: The package does not select HTTP content types, status codes, SOAPAction, JSON-RPC, JSON:API, WSDL, XSD, or registries.
public_apis: Root wire package and all format packages
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9110 is monitored only for the HTTP boundary explicitly excluded from package ownership.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separately specified transport, schema, or application API is proposed.
